claims.claim: Celestica identity/tradability is validated as CLS on NYSE; cumulative Scout/Beta evidence collapses to one issuer-origin Q2 source, so it is primary but not independent corroboration.

A current independent market-cap source reports approximately $41.94B in September 2026, materially above 2025 year-end market capitalization, supporting conservative valuation treatment rather than assuming cheapness from operating growth alone.

provenance.freshness: Q2 primary plus current September market source
provenance.rawVsDerivedConsistency: Q2 revenue/margin/EPS claims match cumulative Scout/Beta packet; no material contradiction found

unknowns.unknown: Exact current enterprise value and forward consensus multiples are not established by the reviewed lawful sources.

claims.claim: Q2 2026 revenue was $4.70B, up 62% year over year; adjusted operating margin was 8.2% and adjusted EPS $2.54 versus $1.39 a year earlier.
Management had already raised 2026 revenue outlook to $19.0B and adjusted EPS to $10.15 after Q1, with unchanged $500M free-cash-flow outlook and improved 2027 visibility/new program wins.

Current market capitalization near $41.94B implies valuation expectations have risen sharply alongside operating momentum; absent source-addressed EV/forward-multiple evidence, valuation is treated as demanding/mixed rather than favorable.

thesisQuality.basis: Exceptional recent demand growth and new-program visibility support durable relevance, but customer/program concentration and substitutability prevent an exceptional band.

financialOperatingMomentum.basis: Revenue +62% YoY with margin and EPS expansion plus raised annual outlook and $500M FCF outlook supports exceptional current momentum.

marketValuationOpportunity.basis: September market cap near $41.94B after a very large multi-year rerating makes valuation demanding relative to incomplete EV/forward-multiple evidence; conservative weak-to-mixed assessment.

catalystScore.basis: Raised 2026 outlook, improved 2027 visibility and new program wins provide multiple material source-supported catalysts, though exact timing/program economics remain incomplete.

governancePower.basis: Primary disclosure is timely and execution against/above guidance is strong, but this run lacks a fresh source-addressed proxy/capital-allocation record sufficient for a strong governance band.

alignment2036.basis: Networking/server manufacturing directly participates in durable AI/data-center infrastructure demand, but is not itself proven foundational or irreplaceable.

crossDivisionLeverage.basis: Program wins and infrastructure exposure show multiple demand channels, while exact customer/division diversification is not quantified in reviewed sources.

bottleneckControl.basis: Celestica participates in constrained high-growth hardware manufacturing but reviewed evidence does not show exclusive control or prohibitive switching costs.

scenarioRobustness.basis: Manufacturing capability can serve multiple infrastructure programs, but customer insourcing, capex normalization and program loss remain material scenario dependencies.

substitutionResilience.basis: Execution and program wins indicate capability, but alternate manufacturers and customer redesign/insourcing remain credible substitutes.

supplyChainResilience.basis: Strong execution through rapid growth is positive operational evidence, but reviewed sources do not establish multi-source/geographic redundancy for critical inputs.

pricingPower.basis: Adjusted operating margin expansion alongside 62% revenue growth supports some value capture, but contract pass-through/scarcity-rent evidence is not established.

riskEvidence.basis: Principal risks are customer/program concentration, insourcing/substitution, capacity execution and valuation expectations after a major rerating; none currently contradict operating momentum.

dataConfidenceEvidence.basis: Strong recent issuer operating evidence plus one independent current valuation source; confidence is reduced by limited independent operating corroboration and unquantified customer/supply/governance details.

scoreRecord.thesis: Celestica is capturing rapid AI/data-center infrastructure demand through networking/server manufacturing with strong operating leverage and program visibility, but value capture remains exposed to customer concentration, substitution and a substantially rerated valuation.
scoreRecord.keyRisk: A major customer/program loss, insourcing shift or capex normalization could compress both growth and utilization while elevated valuation expectations amplify downside.
scoreRecord.nextCatalyst: Execution against the raised 2026 outlook and evidence that new program wins convert into sustained 2027 growth and margins.

scoreBreakdown.note: Weighted Methodology 1.0 component score; canonical engine retains authority for any risk/confidence transformation.

risks.risk: Customer/program concentration and insourcing can interrupt revenue and utilization.
Current valuation embeds materially higher expectations than prior years.

unknowns.unknown: Exact top-customer exposure, contract economics and critical-component redundancy remain unquantified.
Fresh proxy-level governance/capital-allocation detail was not acquired in this run.
